original_question: Can one obtain a complete classification of homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with homogeneous geodesics (g.o. spaces, meaning homogeneous spaces in which every geodesic is an orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of the acting group) in dimension 7 and in all higher dimensions?
target_in_paper: Section 10, "Some open problems": the opening statement that a complete classification of homogeneous g.o. spaces is still unknown in dimension 7, and that a complete classification in any dimension greater than 7 is far from being accomplished. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s main open classification target: homogeneous Riemannian manifolds with homogeneous geodesics (g.o. spaces), and it correctly singles out dimension 7 as the first unresolved case after the known classification up to dimension 6, while also reflecting the broader unresolved status in dimensions greater than 7. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))
missing_details: The paper does not present this as a formal numbered conjecture or theorem; it is phrased as an open classification goal, with a sharper distinction between the two regimes: dimension 7 is still unclassified, while dimensions greater than 7 are described as far from a complete classification. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))

To make the question stand alone, it should specify the geometric setting used throughout the paper: connected homogeneous Riemannian manifolds written as M=G/K, where G is a connected transitive group of isometries and K is an isotropy subgroup. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))

The paper’s precise terminology distinguishes a G-g.o. space from a g.o. manifold: a G-g.o. space is defined relative to a chosen transitive isometry group G, while 'g.o. manifold' refers to the case when G is the full connected isometry group. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))

A paper-faithful formulation should acknowledge the baseline result that complete classification is known only up to dimension 6, which is why the open problem begins at dimension 7. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))

If one wants the mathematically sharp Lie-algebraic version used in the paper, the g.o. condition can be stated via the associated metric operator Λ and a reductive decomposition g=k⊕m: for every x∈m there exists a(x)∈k with [a(x)+x,Λx]∈k. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))

There are no ambient ring/field, polynomial degree, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large' quantifier issues in this problem; the missing information is geometric and Lie-theoretic rather than algebraic. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))
refined_question: Determine all connected 7-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian g.o. spaces (M=G/K,g), meaning those for which every geodesic is an orbit γ(t)=exp(tX)·o of a one-parameter subgroup of a connected transitive isometry group G; more generally, obtain a complete classification of homogeneous Riemannian g.o. spaces in every dimension n>7. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, classify all 7-dimensional—and more generally all n>7-dimensional—connected homogeneous spaces M=G/K with reductive decomposition g=k⊕m and associated metric operator Λ such that for every x∈m there exists a(x)∈k satisfying [a(x)+x,Λx]∈k. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the first open problem stated in Section 10, not the later suggested narrower problem about spaces with two or three irreducible isotropy summands. Section 3 explains why dimension 7 is the relevant threshold: Theorem 3.1 gives the complete classification only up to dimension 6, and Theorem 3.2 exhibits explicit 7-dimensional non-naturally reductive g.o. examples. The opening sentences of Section 10 then state that dimension 7 still lacks a complete classification and that the full classification problem in dimensions greater than 7 is far from solved. Definition 1 and Corollary 2.3 provide the exact notion of a g.o. space and its standard Lie-algebraic reformulation, which makes the rewritten question self-contained and faithful to the paper’s intent. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))
